transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-01-11 14:00 PST
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Dylan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Roberta (Redwood CSM), Samira (Aurora CISO), Ethan (Aurora Head of Platform), Lilly (Aurora Security Engineer), Tom (Aurora DevOps)

Summary section (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood and Aurora align on pilot goals: validate security posture, prove latency and cost targets with sample workload, test SSO/SAML and RBAC, enable audit logs for compliance. Discuss pilot timeline ~4-6 weeks.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Dylan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samira (Aurora): Samira here.
[00:08] Ethan: Ethan on the call.
[00:10] Lilly: Lilly here.
[00:12] Tom: Tom present.
[00:14] Maya (Redwood): Maya, hi.
[00:15] Roberta (Redwood): Roberta.
[00:20] Dylan: Great. For context, this is a POC scoping to run a security pilot — figure out success criteria, workload sizing for your assistant, and the benchmarks we should run. I'll hand it to Maya to outline what we typically do on the infra side.
[00:32] Maya: Thanks. So typically we start with a 24-hour benchmark of your representative traffic, then a targeted latency SLO and cost-per-1000-token target. For healthcare, we also do a privacy audit and make sure our deployment meets SOC two — sometimes the transcript says "SOC too" — and ISO alignment, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs are enabled.
[00:53] Samira: Right, SOC 2 and ISO are must-haves for us. We also need encryption key ownership options — KMS or customer HSM — and clear audit logs for any model access.
[01:05] Dylan: Absolutely. We support customer-managed KMS for Private/Prem options and can surface HSM integrations for enterprise plans. For the hosted pilot we'll provide encrypted-at-rest and in-transit by default and detailed audit traces.
[01:18] Ethan: For success criteria, from product side we need sub-500ms 95th percentile for single-turn queries on the small assistant model and cost under $0.XX per 1k tokens on average. Those numbers are placeholders, but we need to agree on targets.
[01:35] Maya: Yep, and we should scope the workload: concurrent sessions, average token length, and peak QPS. Lilly, can you share your expected numbers?
[01:45] Lilly: Sure — our concierge assistant sees about 1200 interactions per day right now, avg ~220 tokens per interaction, peaks of ~40 concurrent users in business hours. For the pilot we want to simulate production with 2k interactions/day to see scale.
[02:00] Tom: And note we route through an internal proxy today, so network egress rules and VPC peering matter if you do a private deployment.
[02:08] Dylan: Understood. For sizing, that workload suggests we should test with continuous batching enabled and a dedicated pool for the pilot. We'll propose a config in the follow-up.
[02:20] Samira: Security checklist: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, SAML SSO with our IdP (Okta), RBAC with audit trails retained 1 year, ability to do log export to our SIEM, encryption with customer KMS. Anything else?
[02:36] Maya: We also recommend token-level redaction hooks and the ability to exclude PII from logs; we can do prompt-layer redaction and provide a sample redaction policy.
[02:46] Lilly: We need to be explicit on what shows up in audit logs — request payloads, model outputs, which fields are redacted, and who accessed the logs. Also need read-only roles for compliance auditors.
[02:58] Dylan: Good point. We'll include RBAC roles: admin, developer, auditor, and a limited-service account. We'll document which role can see raw payloads vs redacted entries.
[03:10] Ethan: On the benchmarks, can we run both hosted and a private deployment? We want to compare latency/cost differences and failover behavior.
[03:19] Maya: Yes. For hosted we can run a representative 24h benchmark against our hosted API with prefix caching enabled; for private we can spin up a trial cluster in your VPC (if network ops allows) and run the same workload. There may be slight differences due to network hops and instance sizing.
[03:34] Tom: Our network team prefers VPC peering and private deployment for PHI-sensitive flows. For the pilot, can Redwood provide a private control plane option?
[03:42] Dylan: We offer a private deployment option for pilots on enterprise terms; control plane remains customer-managed in the Private offering. For the POC we can do hosted with VPC peering or a short-lived private deployment depending on paperwork speed.
[03:55] Samira: Paperwork — we need an NDA and a DPA; also access to your SOC2 audit.
[04:01] Roberta: We'll push the SOC2 Type II report and the security pack to the shared folder after this call, and include our DPA template.
[04:09] Samira: Great. On timelines — we were thinking a 4-6 week pilot: week 1 integration (SSO + sample data), week 2 benchmark and baseline, week 3 tuning and RBAC/audit validation, week 4 internal compliance review and sign-off. Does that sound doable?
[04:23] Dylan: Yes that's consistent. We'll propose a more granular plan in the follow up.
[04:28] Ethan: For cost modeling, we want an estimate for both hosted and dedicated pools at your suggested config. Also need quantization/precision tradeoffs — will 8-bit quantization be acceptable for our accuracy needs?
[04:40] Maya: We'll run evals with 8-bit and 16-bit quant profiles and report model/regression delta. For some models the quality drop is minimal; we'll include that in benchmark report.
[04:52] Lilly: One more security ask — SAML assertion lifetime and session token expiration control; we need session revocation capability.
[04:59] Maya: We support configurable session TTLs and can align with your IdP session settings; revocation will be part of the admin console — we can demo that.
[05:09] Tom: On audit logs export, does Redwood push logs to an S3 bucket in our account or pull from your side?
[05:16] Dylan: We can do both. For Private deployments we can write logs to your S3 (or GCS/Azure) or stream to your SIEM via syslog/Kinesis. For Hosted we provide a secure export endpoint and can forward to your SIEM with customer-managed keys.
[05:30] Samira: We will want a field-level mapping of what is exported. Provide a sample audit schema please.
[05:36] Maya: I'll include the schema in the security pack; it'll show which fields are raw vs redacted and retention windows.
[05:43] Ethan: On stakeholders, compliance will review the SOC docs and logs; platform will test the SSO and run the benchmarks. We should define acceptance criteria: e.g., 95th %-ile latency < 500ms (single-turn), no PII in logs beyond redaction policy, successful SAML auth for all test accounts, RBAC roles validated by audit team.
[06:05] Dylan: Good, we'll codify that as the success criteria in the POC statement of work.
[06:10] Samira: Any legal concerns about data residency? Some of our PHI must remain in-region.
[06:15] Dylan: We have regional hosted clusters; for strict residency we recommend Private deployment in your region or dedicated capacity. We'll map options in the follow-up.
[06:25] Roberta: Action items recap: we'll send security pack and SOC2; Redwood will send integration guide and SAML test plan; Aurora to send representative payloads and test accounts.
[06:40] Dylan: One quick note on transcription — sometimes Redwood product names get munged in auto-notes; we mentioned KV cache and sometimes it shows as "KV cash" in auto transcripts.
[06:48] Lilly: Ha, yes the auto transcription often mangles model names.
[06:52] Maya: We'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet template.
[06:55] Tom: Lastly, on monitoring — how granular are the telemetry hooks? We need per-request tracing, token-level latency histograms and per-route cost breakdowns.
[07:06] Maya: We provide per-route dashboards, token and request histograms, and per-key cost breakdowns in the console; we can also stream metrics to your monitoring stack (Prometheus/Grafana) for long-term retention.
[07:18] Samira: Ok that's helpful. If you can deliver the security pack and SOC2 artifacts by Friday we can start the internal sign-offs.
[07:24] Dylan: We'll aim for that. Any final questions?
[07:29] Ethan: No, just next steps on scheduling the SSO test.
[07:33] Dylan: Maya and Tom will coordinate via email to set the SAML metadata exchange; Roberta will share the DPA and SOC2 link.
[07:40] Roberta: I'll create a shared Google folder and drop the docs, plus the benchmark sample sheet.
[07:45] Samira: Thanks everyone.
[07:47] Dylan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the plan and dates.

End of transcript.
